articles.title: A Texas inheritance battle over family ranches, bank accounts, a yacht and luxury vehicles led to a court freeze backed by a $1 million bond; appeals judges have narrowed how broadly it can apply
articles.summary: A Texas family fight over an inheritance involving ranches, bank accounts, a private yacht, aircraft and luxury vehicles is heading back to court.
articles.body: A Texas family fight over an inheritance involving ranches, bank accounts, a private yacht, aircraft and luxury vehicles is heading back to court. An appeals panel ruled that parts of an asset freeze were too broad and unclear. The Texas Second Court of Appeals issued its decision on 19 November 2026 in the estate of Lonnie K. Ledbetter Jr. The ruling kept part of a second temporary court order in place while throwing out other parts. That order blocked his wife, Tawni Ledbetter, and others from using or moving property tied to the estate and family trusts.This legal battle involves a $1 million bond, a court-appointed manager and repeated arguments over how much control Tawni should have over the family's money and property. The appeals judges decided that the freeze can stay in place for clearly named bank accounts and specific items. However, they said the order cannot cover property that was not clearly listed. This decision came after an earlier appeal where the same court threw out parts of a first freeze because its wording was too vague and wide-ranging. Once again, the appeals court told the lower court to spell out the exact property and actions covered by the order.Family dispute centres on estate and trust assetsThe case deals with the estate of Lonnie K. Ledbetter Jr. After he died, two of his children, Lonnie K. Ledbetter III, known as Trace, and Kendall Ledbetter Hohmann, sued Tawni. According to the court's earlier December 2025 decision, Trace and Kendall claimed their father did not have the mental or legal ability to sign key papers after he married Tawni. They also argued that she unfairly pressured him into signing those documents. The fight centers on changes to his estate and trust plans, including requests to recognize an older will and a 2021 update in probate court.The appeals court's December 2025 ruling noted that the children wanted to protect money and property belonging to their father's estate and the Ledbetter family trusts while the main lawsuit plays out. The court agreed they had shown a strong legal claim and a real danger that the money could be spent or lost. The contested property goes far beyond regular cash and real estate. It includes ranches in Texas, a property in Florida, a yacht, aircraft, cars, horses, business shares and several bank and investment accounts.The court's December 2025 opinion also listed major purchases made after Lonnie married Tawni. Those items included a private jet estimated to cost between $6 million and $7 million and a yacht worth around $5 million. A jointly owned ranch was also put up for sale for about $18 million. In addition, the court pointed out that Tawni bought property in Florida worth roughly $6 million after the marriage. In earlier court testimony, she first denied getting money from Lonnie or his companies to buy that property. Later, she admitted using several million dollars that came from him or his businesses.Court appoints receiver to manage the assetsIn May 2025, a Hood County court issued its first temporary freeze, stopping Tawni and others from using or moving certain estate and trust assets. The next month, the judge named Catherine Goodman as a receiver to take charge of the trust property. As receiver, Goodman got the power to pay regular bills needed to own, protect, insure and run the properties. This step mattered because the estate held costly homes and businesses that needed steady spending to stay in good shape.In its December 2025 ruling, the Texas Second Court of Appeals threw out large sections of that first freeze. The judges said several rules were too vague because they talked about assets, funds and accounts in general terms without naming them clearly. The court also noted that the order failed to properly allow for basic payments needed to maintain the properties. That earlier ruling showed just how expensive it was to keep the family's holdings running. Testimony revealed that the yacht cost around $70,000 a month for its crew, plus dock fees of between $18,000 and $25,000. The ranch also held more than 100 horses, costing roughly $183,000 a month to care for.An earlier temporary order had let Tawni spend up to $300,000 on needed costs, but that allowance was left out of the first freeze. Because of that, the appeals judges ruled that the restrictions went too far by blocking payments needed to keep the property running. After that first appeal, Trace and Kendall asked the lower court for clearer, more specific limits. The Hood County judge held a hearing on 19 December 2025 and issued a second temporary freeze.Second asset freeze includes bank accounts and luxury propertyThis second court order gave a detailed list of properties and accounts that Tawni, her children and certain businesses were barred from accessing, moving, selling, spending or hiding. The listed real estate included two addresses on Meander Road in Granbury, Texas, and a property on River Road on Ono Island, Alabama. It also covered a house in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and several family-linked business shares.The vehicle list named a 2020 Bentley Continental, a 2004 Dodge Viper, a 1987 Porsche, a 2024 Foretravel Presidential RV, a 2021 GMC Sierra 1500 and a 2022 Jeep Gladiator. Several motorcycles, boats and jet skis were listed as well. Other frozen items included a Dassault Falcon 900 private jet, a Bell helicopter, the Kashmir Yacht and ownership shares in several ranching and aviation businesses. The order also kept in place a $1 million bond that Trace and Kendall had already posted. The trial judge said that money would protect Tawni and the affected companies from financial loss until the case is finally decided.Appeals court examines financial concernsDuring the December 2025 hearing, lawyers shared new details about how the family's cash and companies were being handled. According to the November 2026 appeals court opinion, Tawni admitted moving $3.5 million from accounts belonging to Lonnie's estate into her son's account after the first freeze had already been ordered. Receiver Catherine Goodman also testified that she was told the various businesses needed about $150,000 a month to run. Yet she had spent nearly $1.4 million between September and December 2025 on needed bills and payments to outside parties.Goodman raised red flags about company payroll as well. One company had a regular payroll of around $18,000 every two weeks, but she found at least five payouts of roughly $57,000 each that were made without her knowing. She also told the court that some payments were handed out in cash, with records showing Tawni received them. In addition, some workers were paid through bank accounts outside the receiver's control. Goodman said Tawni kept unauthorized view-only access to some accounts even after the earlier court limits took effect. Eventually, Goodman moved the accounts to a different financial adviser to keep a closer watch on the money.Appeals court keeps some restrictions in placeIn its 19 November 2026 ruling, the Texas Second Court of Appeals agreed with Tawni that parts of the second freeze were still too broad. The judges pointed out that using the word "including" let the order stretch to extra properties, accounts and business tasks that were never clearly named. The panel ruled that anyone bound by a court freeze must be able to see exactly what they cannot do without having to guess. As a result, the judges threw out limits on assets and activities that were not spelled out clearly.At the same time, the court kept the freeze in place for bank accounts listed with their bank names, account numbers and account holders. The judges also rejected Tawni's claim that the whole order was invalid because the lower court did not set a brand-new bond. The appeals court confirmed that the original $1 million bond still covered the second order. It also turned down her challenges to the lower court's power to hear the case and the children's legal right to ask for protection.Tawni had also argued that some of the frozen property belonged to her before she married Lonnie. She estimated that she brought about $4 million in cash and property into the marriage. However, the court noted that she failed to show bank statements, transfer records or tax papers to back up her claim. Because of that lack of proof, the judges refused to lift the freeze on the clearly named properties and accounts. In the end, the court upheld part of the second freeze and threw out part of it. It kept limits on clearly named accounts while canceling limits on unnamed property and business actions, sending the case back to the lower court for the next steps. Justice Brian Walker wrote the opinion, joined by Chief Justice Sudderth and Justice Womack. The ruling leaves the court-appointed receiver in charge of the listed businesses and their daily running costs while the larger inheritance fight moves forward.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK, Netherlands push for 'lasting peace' in Ukraine, vow to keep pressure on Putin
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten met on Saturday and committed to continuing support for Ukraine as it defends
articles.body: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten met on Saturday and committed to continuing support for Ukraine as it defends itself against Russia's invasion. The two leaders also stressed the need to maintain pressure on Moscow to bring Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table, Downing Street said in a statement."Both leaders agreed on the vital need to keep the pressure up on Russia to bring (Russian President Vladimir) Putin to the negotiations table," the statement said.The meeting came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated that NATO membership remained the strongest security guarantee for his country. He also argued that Ukraine's inclusion in the alliance would strengthen NATO itself.Zelenskyy says NATO membership is clearest security guaranteeIn a post on X, Zelenskyy said Ukraine's NATO membership was discussed during the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin."The Allies understand that the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine is NATO membership. And the clearest way to strengthen NATO is to bring Ukraine in," he wrote.Addressing proposals for security guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5, which provides for collective defence, Zelenskyy said Kyiv still lacked clarity on how such arrangements would work.He questioned whether countries offering such guarantees would be prepared to defend Ukraine if Russia launched another attack."For Ukraine, it's not clear yet, because we still don't have a full answer about what this collective would be, how it would defend us, and whether it would be ready to repel the aggressor," he said.He stressed that any alternative arrangement must be backed by clear commitments in writing."The answers should not just be words – this has to be on paper," Zelenskyy stated.The Ukrainian president also said the guarantees must remain effective beyond US President Donald Trump's tenure. He argued that Ukraine needed long-term protection rather than a temporary arrangement."We need security guarantees not for two years, but forever," he said.Zelenskyy warned that a security arrangement lasting only two years would offer a temporary pause in the conflict rather than lasting peace.Zelenskyy says Putin failed to achieve 'Yalta 2'Zelenskyy also said Putin had failed to achieve what he described as his plan to redraw international borders and divide the world into spheres of influence.Referring to the recent engagement between the United States and Russia, he said Ukraine was not discussed and no public outcome suggested that an agreement on redrawing borders had been reached.He also said China had not allowed itself to be drawn into such an arrangement."If there really was an intention to reaffirm the victory over fascism now, then the participants at this summit would have to be the United States, Europe, and Ukraine. Definitely not Russia," he said.Zelenskyy described the trilateral summit as a setback for Moscow. He also linked Russia's subsequent military action to its failure to secure the outcome it wanted.He cited an overnight Russian attack involving 111 missiles against Ukraine."If Putin wanted to remind the world once again who he is, there was no need – we haven't forgotten that he's a terrorist and a killer," he wrote.Zelenskyy thanks Melania Trump for evacuation effortsSeparately, Zelenskyy thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for helping facilitate the evacuation of people from Oleshky.He said he had discussed further humanitarian evacuation operations with Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapatyi. They had also approved an updated list of settlements where similar operations could be carried out.The proposed evacuation locations include Radensk, Kostohryzove, Hola Prystan, Stara Zburivka, Nova Zburivka, Hladkivka, Velyki Kopani, Kardashynka and Velyka Kardashynka in the Kherson region.In the Zaporizhzhia region, the list includes Mayachka, Zlatopil, Dniprorudne, Kamyanske, Verkhnia Krynytsia and Vasylivka.Zelenskyy said the updated list had been shared with Ukraine's ombudsman and the US side. He added that it would be revised further.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An American artist united more than 2,300 stitchers to create a 25-million-stitch installation representing the global refugee crisis, with each stitch symbolising one refugee
articles.summary: An unusual art project has turned the global refugee crisis into a large embroidery installation, with each stitch representing one refugee.
articles.body: An unusual art project has turned the global refugee crisis into a large embroidery installation, with each stitch representing one refugee. Titled ‘25 Million Stitches: One Stitch, One Refugee', the project was started by Sacramento-based Korean-American fibre artist Jennifer Kim Sohn. It brought together over 2,300 stitchers who contributed embroidered fabric panels to represent the figure of 25 million displaced people.According to the Mingei International Museum, Sohn was inspired to start the project after reading a 2019 report by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, which put the number of refugees worldwide at more than 25 million. The contributors created over 2,000 panels, which were joined vertically to form 408 floor-to-ceiling flags.How the Syrian refugee crisis inspired the 25 Million Stitches projectSohn said the original idea began after she read about the Syrian refugee crisis in The New York Times in 2013. Stories about children being put on boats by parents who knew they could not accompany them affected her deeply. She began researching refugees around the world and later came across a 2019 report by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.It stated that there were more than 25 million refugees worldwide, most of whom Sohn described as climate refugees. She felt that 25 million was such a huge number that people would find it difficult to understand how many people it represented. Having seen art used to present data, she believed that a visual representation of the figure could help people grasp its scale and make a strong impact.Social media helped turn the artwork into a community projectSohn initially tried to complete the project herself using a sewing machine. However, the machine broke after three and a half days, leaving her with just 16 inches by 40 feet of stitching. She then realised that the project was too big to handle alone and reached out to neighbourhood groups and artists for help. She also began sharing the project on social media, but people were slow to join because they knew how long it would take to stitch a 64-inch panel.Sohn continued spreading the word and gradually received more contributions. The project gained momentum during the COVID-19 pandemic, when people were looking for ways to connect with others while staying apart. The group collected 23 million stitches in just two months.How a solo embroidery idea became a global community projectMore than 2,300 stitchers took part in the project and helped shape the final artwork. Sohn had initially planned to create one huge piece made entirely of running stitches. However, as more people joined, they added their own designs and messages to the fabric panels, changing her original idea. She also wanted the artwork to be large but easy to transport.This led her to choose embroidery on fabric rather than a heavier material. She considered both fabric and paper but chose muslin because it was more durable and easier to transport. Stitching also had a deeper meaning for her. She saw it as a traditional way of repairing things, such as holes in socks and pockets, instead of buying new clothes.The message behind the 25 Million Stitches installationSohn said she hoped the project would encourage people to see refugees as neighbours and fellow human beings, rather than as a threat to limited resources. The exhibition was designed as an immersive experience for visitors. More than 2,000 embroidered panels are joined vertically to create 408 flags, which hang from the ceiling. Visitors can walk through and around the suspended installation.Sohn said the project had already affected many people. She recalled visitors approaching her with tears in their eyes and hugging her after seeing the exhibition. articles.title: Ladakh chief secretary cites cites 70% panchayat poll turnout, sticks to December 4 hill council voting
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the high voter turnout in panchayat and municipal elections held the previous day,
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the high voter turnout in panchayat and municipal elections held the previous day, saying it reflected that people want democracy as he appealed for greater participation in hill council (LAHDC) polls scheduled for Dec 4.The turnout was 70.03% in Saturday’s panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal polls. “We must not forget that the last panchayat and municipal elections were held in 2018. This is the first time elections are being held since Ladakh became a Union Territory (in 2019),” Kundra said.Kundra announced that talks between Ladakhi representatives and the Union home ministry (MHA) on autonomy would resume after the LAHDC elections. Leh Apex Body (LAH) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk is at the forefront of protests by Ladakhi groups against holding the LAHDC polls in the harsh winter when they claim many people are away.Kundra asked Wangchuk not to make “provocative statements” during election season. Asked about LAB’s demand to delay LAHDC polls, Kundra said: “Only 10 to 12 days are left. Around 70% of the people voted in the panchayat election. To claim that 40% of the people are not even here is not correct. It is not as if people are casting their votes without being present.”Kundra urged Ladakhi representatives not to outrightly reject proposals on the table during talks with MHA teams, stressing that the Centre was committed to providing the best possible solution under Article 371 for the people of the region. The talks with LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) will resume once the elections are over, Kundra said. “The dialogue is political. Anything that can influence the outcome cannot be undertaken during the election process,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Atlanta's abandoned prison farm, with crumbling buildings and a former zoo-animal cemetery, could become a public park and memorial; the city has unveiled plans but must first relocate a bomb range
articles.summary: Some places carry histories that cannot simply be erased by the passage of time.
articles.body: Some places carry histories that cannot simply be erased by the passage of time. Their walls, abandoned structures and forgotten corners often hold memories of lives and experiences that deserve to be remembered. Yet, as cities grow and landscapes change, these places sometimes find new purposes, offering an opportunity to preserve the past while making room for the future.In Atlanta, an abandoned prison farm that once stood as a site of confinement could soon take on a very different identity. The city has unveiled plans to transform the historic property into a public park and memorial, with crumbling buildings and even a cemetery for former zoo animals forming part of its unusual history. However, before the proposed transformation can move forward, the city must first address a significant obstacle: relocating a bomb detonation range operating on the property.According to a report by Marisa Mecke, published by WABE on November 18, 2026, the City of Atlanta's Department of Parks and Recreation has unveiled the final design for the proposed Restoration Memorial & Preserve at the former Atlanta Prison Farm site. The project aims to preserve the property's historical significance while transforming the remaining undeveloped land into a public green space, with plans for walking trails, a museum, a nature centre and spaces for reflection. However, the proposal faces several hurdles before it can become a reality, including the relocation of a bomb detonation range currently operating on the property.Explaining the historical significance of the proposed memorial, Matthew Cartledge, a landscape architect with HGOR, told WABE, “You know, everybody knows about the Civil War, we all know about the Civil Rights Era, but there’s this whole period in here that’s sort of forgotten, right?”The forgotten history behind Atlanta's abandoned prison farmThe history of the Atlanta Prison Farm stretches back much further than its abandoned buildings might suggest. The land originally belonged to the Muscogee people before passing into private ownership and eventually being acquired by the City of Atlanta in 1911. Initially intended for a crematory, the property was later operated as a municipal dairy farm before being converted into a prison farm in the mid-1920s.The prison farm housed people incarcerated by the city, many of whom were made to work on the agricultural property. Their labour helped produce food and dairy for city institutions, while prisoners were also assigned work on other municipal projects. The facility continued operating for several decades before closing in the mid-1990s. Today, its remaining buildings and overgrown landscape stand as reminders of a largely overlooked chapter in Atlanta's history.What Atlanta's proposed park and memorial will look likeThe proposed transformation of the Atlanta Prison Farm is centred on preserving the site's historical remains while giving the surrounding community access to a new public green space. The final design, developed by the City of Atlanta's Department of Parks and Recreation in collaboration with landscape design firm HGOR, includes plans to preserve some of the old prison buildings and create dedicated spaces for reflection and remembrance.The proposed facilities include a museum, a nature centre, walking trails, an outdoor classroom, a community garden, picnic areas and an accessible playground. The design also incorporates natural-surface trails and open green spaces, with the landscape becoming progressively less developed as visitors move away from the entrance towards the wooded areas of the property.The memorial is also part of a broader effort by the city to acknowledge the history of forced convict labour at several sites across Atlanta, including the Chattahoochee Brick Site and Bellwood Quarry. Through these projects, the city hopes to connect historical remembrance with environmental restoration and public recreation.For now, the future of the Atlanta Prison Farm remains tied to a number of practical challenges, particularly the relocation of the bomb detonation range and the work required to make the property suitable for public use. However, the proposed transformation represents an opportunity to give a long-overlooked site a new purpose without erasing the history it carries. If realised, the project could allow future generations to explore its natural landscape, learn about a difficult chapter in Atlanta's past and reflect on the people whose labour shaped the city's history. It is a reminder that preserving a place does not always mean leaving it untouched; sometimes, it means finding a way to remember its past while making it accessible to the future.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Every American with a retirement account is in the blast radius’: DOJ targets Chinese crypto scam network, freezes $52 million and shuts 13 compounds in Madagascar
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice has announced a major crackdown on cryptocurrency-related fraud networks allegedly run by Chinese organised crime groups,
articles.body: The US Department of Justice has announced a major crackdown on cryptocurrency-related fraud networks allegedly run by Chinese organised crime groups, with authorities restraining approximately $52 million in cryptocurrency in a single day and assisting local law enforcement in shutting down 13 scam compounds in Madagascar.US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro announced the coordinated action by the Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, working alongside the Department of the Treasury, the FBI and the US Secret Service. The latest seizures bring the total value of cryptocurrency restrained by the Strike Force to approximately $938 million.The operation targeted Xinbi Guarantee, also known as Xinbi, a Chinese-language illicit marketplace allegedly used by scam operators to access money-laundering services, fraudulent investment websites and even people trafficked into scam compounds across Southeast Asia.US authorities target Xinbi's alleged role in crypto fraudAccording to a seizure warrant unsealed by the Justice Department, Xinbi operated primarily through Telegram, where vendors advertised services to scam centre operators. These allegedly included setting up fake investment websites, laundering money obtained from victims of wire fraud and recruiting trafficking victims to work in scam compounds.The marketplace reportedly acted as an intermediary, holding payments until vendors completed the services purchased by scammers. Investigators traced funds belonging to American fraud victims to cryptocurrency wallets advertised by vendors on the platform.A US District Court for the District of Columbia authorised the seizure of Telegram channels hosting the marketplace on September 7, 2026.As part of the operation, law enforcement seized two cryptocurrency wallets allegedly used by Xinbi to collect vendor payments. The wallets collectively held approximately $12 million. Authorities also sought to restrain 47 additional wallets believed to be connected to money laundering on Xinbi's network.The coordinated action resulted in more than $52 million in cryptocurrency being restrained. The Justice Department also acknowledged Tether for its assistance in the investigation.Treasury sanctions Xinbi and two other entitiesIn a parallel move, the US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated Xinbi as a significant transnational criminal organisation. It also identified several cryptocurrency wallets associated with the marketplace.Two other entities were sanctioned for allegedly providing financial, material or technological support, or goods and services, to Xinbi.Under the sanctions, all property and interests in property belonging to the designated entities that are within the United States or in the possession or control of US persons are blocked. Such assets must also be reported to OFAC.Pirro said the crackdown was aimed at dismantling the criminal networks and the services that help them operate.“If Chinese organised crime can buy a custom website and a money laundering service the way you order takeout, then every American with a retirement account is in the blast radius,” Pirro said. She added that the Strike Force would continue targeting Chinese organised crime groups and those who facilitate their activities.US team assists in shutting down 13 scam compounds in MadagascarAlongside the action against Xinbi, Pirro announced that the Scam Center Strike Force was expanding its operations beyond Southeast Asia to target scam compounds around the world.As part of this wider effort, a team from the Strike Force travelled to Madagascar and spent two weeks assisting local authorities in operations against 13 scam centres allegedly run by Chinese organised crime syndicates.The team helped process more than 3,200 electronic devices and conducted interviews with nearly 400 people who had been arrested. The investigations have also led to new inquiries by US authorities. The Justice Department said at least approximately 30 Chinese nationals identified as leaders of the compounds were repatriated to China by the Chinese government.US Attorney for the District of Alaska Michael J. Heyman and FBI Criminal Division Deputy Assistant Director Matthew Floyd joined Pirro in announcing the deployment.“Transnational criminal organisations don’t care about borders, and the Department of Justice won’t either,” Heyman said, adding that the authorities would work to dismantle international scam networks and pursue justice for American fraud victims.Cryptocurrency investment scams cost Americans billionsThe Scam Center Strike Force was launched in November 2025 to tackle the growing threat of Chinese organised crime groups operating scam centres, particularly in Southeast Asia. Its investigations cover cryptocurrency investment fraud, cyber-enabled scams, human trafficking and money laundering.According to figures cited by the Justice Department from the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), cryptocurrency investment fraud losses reported to the agency rose from $4.57 billion in 2023 to $8.65 billion in 2025, an increase of 89%.The department also said cyber-enabled fraud accounted for almost 85% of all losses reported to IC3 in 2025. It cautioned that the actual financial damage could be significantly higher because many victims do not report scams to authorities.The Strike Force brings together several federal agencies, including the FBI, the US Secret Service, the Justice Department's Criminal Division, the US Postal Inspection Service, IRS Criminal Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations. It also works with the Treasury and State Departments, as well as private-sector partners.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Goldie Hawn joined more than 1,700 people at an Atlanta charity luncheon on November 19; the event raised $1,086,250 for programmes supporting women and girls, including a $500,000 corporate matching gift
articles.summary: A charity luncheon celebrating women and girls brought together Hollywood actor Goldie Hawn and more than 1,700 attendees in Atlanta, raising over $1
articles.body: A charity luncheon celebrating women and girls brought together Hollywood actor Goldie Hawn and more than 1,700 attendees in Atlanta, raising over $1 million for community programmes. The 30th annual Numbers Too Big To Ignore Luncheon, organised by the Atlanta Women's Foundation, featured conversations about parenting, kindness, joy and children's mental health. According to the foundation's official website, the annual event is its signature fundraiser, supporting initiatives that help women and girls across metro Atlanta build healthier and more financially secure lives.Held on November 19, 2026, at the Georgia World Congress Center, the luncheon raised $1,086,250 for nonprofit programmes benefiting women and girls. As reported by SaportaReport, the amount included $586,250 collected through donations and a $500,000 matching contribution from The Coca-Cola Foundation. Entertainer and auctioneer Dean Crownover encouraged attendees to contribute, while television journalist Condace Pressley led the conversation with Hawn.Goldie Hawn discusses joy, parenting and kindnessDuring the event, Hawn shared personal experiences and reflections on raising children with her longtime partner, Kurt Russell. She spoke about the importance of emotional well-being, positive parenting and demonstrating kindness through everyday actions. Hawn explained that children learn important values by observing the behaviour of adults around them. She said parenting should focus on teaching love, responsibility, self-respect and good citizenship rather than concentrating only on future success.She also encouraged parents to listen to children and model the behaviour they want them to develop. According to SaportaReport, Hawn emphasised that kindness begins with how people treat themselves and others. The actor also spoke about the importance of joy, describing it as something people carry within themselves rather than an emotion dependent on circumstances. She recalled reminding her children on gloomy mornings that the sun was still shining above the clouds, even when they could not see it.Hawn also shared a childhood experience that influenced her understanding of fear and anxiety. She recalled watching films about atomic bomb explosions at school and becoming frightened whenever she heard the noon whistle. Hawn said that, after the September 11 attacks, she thought about children's vulnerability to anxiety, fear and uncertainty. She was working on an HBO documentary about happiness at the time, but instead founded The Goldie Hawn Foundation, which developed MindUP.How MindUP supports children's mental well-beingHawn founded The Goldie Hawn Foundation in 2003, which developed MindUP, a programme designed to help children build mental fitness and emotional resilience. The initiative brings together approaches informed by neuroscience, psychology and education. It teaches children skills such as emotional regulation, stress management, empathy and concentration.The Atlanta Women's Foundation's official website explains that MindUP has expanded internationally and now reaches more than seven million children across 48 countries. The programme also offers resources for parents, teachers and children to support mental well-being. During the luncheon, Hawn discussed how concerns about children's vulnerability to anxiety and uncertainty helped inspire her work. She said that managing negative emotions is important for creating a healthier environment for future generations.What the $1 million fundraiser will supportThe Numbers Too Big To Ignore Luncheon is the Atlanta Women's Foundation's annual fundraising event, with proceeds supporting nonprofit organisations working with women and girls across metro Atlanta. According to the foundation, its funding priorities include education, housing, healthcare, workforce development and mental health. Its initiatives include All Girls Forward, the Two-Generation Initiative and its Mental Health and Wellbeing Initiative.The organisation said it has invested more than $34.3 million in programmes and community partners since its founding in 1998. The 2026 gathering marked the 30th edition of the luncheon, which has previously featured speakers including Maya Angelou, Gloria Steinem, Jane Fonda and Hoda Kotb.Hawn's appearance brought together her work in entertainment and children's mental health with the foundation's wider mission of supporting women and girls. The fundraising total of $1,086,250 reflected contributions from attendees and the corporate matching gift, helping finance programmes aimed at improving opportunities, well-being and economic security across the Atlanta region.You use AI every day.
